name: Plasma Mobile
summary: Free touch interface and mobile application ecosystem developed by the KDE community, founded on the KWin Wayland compositor and the Qt/Kirigami libraries.
license: Open Source (GPL, LGPL and free KDE licences)

content.introduction: Plasma Mobile is a free initiative of the international KDE community aiming to provide a touch user interface and a complete application environment for smartphones and tablets.
content.what_is_it: Developed since 2015 on the foundations of the KDE Plasma desktop environment, Plasma Mobile adapts the KDE graphical and software stack to mobile form factors without breaking with the traditional Linux ecosystem.
content.desktop_heritage_and_wayland_stack: Plasma Mobile adapts the proven technologies of KDE Plasma Desktop to the ergonomic and hardware constraints of smartphones and touch tablets. The environment runs natively above the KWin Wayland compositor, configured to handle modern touch interaction protocols (wl_touch, text-input-v3 for virtual input with Maliit Keyboard) and dynamic screen orientation switching. The mobile shell presents an interface articulated around a retractable top panel (grouping system notifications and quick settings), a bottom navigation bar with a task manager in the form of application preview cards, and a paginated application launcher.
content.kirigami_framework_and_adaptive_apps: At the heart of the Plasma Mobile ecosystem lies Kirigami, a user interface component library based on Qt Quick / QML developed by the KDE community. Kirigami is designed to create convergent applications capable of dynamically adapting their presentation between a compact format on a smartphone screen and an extended display on a monitor or tablet when the device is connected to a docking station. The ecosystem includes a collection of coordinated native applications: the Angelfish web browser, the Index file manager, the Elisa audio player, the Koko image gallery, the Kalendar agenda, as well as the NeoChat (Matrix) and Tokodon (Mastodon) messaging clients, all benefiting from the Breeze visual consistency.
content.telephony_audio_and_hardware_integration: For the management of telephony and wireless features, Plasma Mobile interfaces with the underlying software layers of the embedded Linux world. Voice telephony, SMS sending and cellular connectivity are managed by the ModemManager daemon (or oFono depending on the distribution) and the Plasma Phonebook / Dialler application. The routing and control of audio flows (switching between internal earpiece, main speaker, wired headset and Bluetooth HSP/HFP profile) are ensured by the PipeWire multimedia server and its WirePlumber session manager. Electrical power management relies on the power-profiles-daemon daemon and deep sleep mechanisms (suspend-to-RAM assisted by microcontroller Crust on Allwinner chips), crucial for preserving the battery life of mobile terminals.
content.technical_constraints_and_limits: It is important to distinguish Plasma Mobile (which is a user interface environment and an application suite) from the complete operating system that hosts it. Plasma Mobile is not distributed in the form of a stand-alone system, but is packaged by independent mobile Linux distributions such as Nura (ex-postmarketOS, on an Alpine Linux foundation with mainline kernels), Mobian (on a Debian GNU/Linux foundation) and Manjaro ARM. If the project works maturely on community development devices such as the PinePhone, the PinePhone Pro and the Volla Phone, its daily use on consumer smartphones ported from Android (OnePlus 6/6T, Xiaomi Pocophone F1) remains subject to hardware limitations: high power consumption in standby, camera hardware acceleration drivers still experimental and absence of a banking ecosystem or of proprietary commercial applications dependent on Google Play services.
content.distribution_and_installation: Plasma Mobile is distributed in the form of packages or images by several distributions, listed on the official "Getting Plasma Mobile" page. Nura (ex-postmarketOS) provides prebuilt images and, for devices not covered, a manual installation through pmbootstrap. Debian and Mobian publish flashable images with Plasma Mobile, in stable version and in weekly images taken from testing; the `plasma-mobile` package is available in Debian and Arch Linux. openSUSE provides Tumbleweed builds for the PinePhone, Fedora an official KDE Mobile spin, and KDE neon an image intended for non-Android Intel tablets, PCs and virtual machines. Custom images can be tested in QEMU.
content.release_trains_and_independent_software_: The post of 8 July 2025 accompanying the July independent releases specifies that most of the Plasma Mobile software is from now on published within the framework of the Plasma or KDE Gear release cycles, and that the archives of these versions are signed. The releases are dated by the KDE announcements of Plasma 6.4 on 17 June 2025, Plasma 6.5 on 21 October 2025, Plasma 6.6 on 17 February 2026 and Plasma 6.7 on 16 June 2026. The post "Plasma Mobile 6.5", dated 10 November 2025, details the changes brought to the mobile components after the release of Plasma 6.5: configuration and activation of the Waydroid container from the settings application and the quick settings panel, loading of the lock screen by reusing the processes of the status bar and of the actions drawer, double tap to lock on the Folio home screen. The posts of November 2025 and December 2025 document the independent versions of Plasma Camera and Plasma Settings, with their archives published separately. The post of 14 August 2024 announces the release of Plasma Dialer 24.08, based on Qt6, with a package deposited on download.kde.org and signed by a GPG key.
content.security_advisory_and_disclosure_flow: Security questions relating to the software produced by KDE, including the Plasma Mobile components, are handled according to the KDE security policy. The page kde.org/info/security consulted on 19 October 2026 asks for them to be addressed to security@kde.org, reserves sysadmin@kde.org for software used but not produced by KDE, and indicates that the reported problems are checked with the author or the maintainer of the code concerned. The policy specifies that release coordinators and distributors packaging the software are informed as soon as a fix is available, so that they prepare their binary packages, then that security advisories are published on kde.org/info/security, with the fixes as source and the binaries available. The page consulted also specifies that KDE does not have a bug bounty programme. The advisories listed as of 19 October 2026 are classified by product: two advisories from 2018 designate Plasma Desktop and Plasma, none designates by name Plasma Mobile, Plasma Camera, Plasma Settings, Plasma Dialer or Plasma Phonebook.
advantages: Fully free and modular user interface stemming from the KDE community
Native Wayland display stack driven by the KWin compositor with hardware acceleration
Kirigami application framework offering convergence between mobile and desktop environments
Compatibility with desktop Linux applications and support for Android containers through Waydroid
Absence of proprietary telemetry and full auditability of the source code
disadvantages: Dependence on host distributions and on the hardware support of the Linux kernel drivers
Increased energy consumption in standby compared with closed mobile systems on the market
Native touch application ecosystem smaller than the dominant commercial platforms
Integration of complex camera sensors and cellular audio hardware still variable depending on the devices
who_is_it_for: Users of stand-alone Linux phones (PinePhone, PinePhone Pro, Librem 5, Nura (ex-postmarketOS) terminals)
Qt, QML and KDE developers wishing to design convergent multiplatform applications
Administrators and free software enthusiasts looking for an open and inspectable mobile stack
who_is_it_not_for: Users requiring immediate support for all banking services under Google Play Protect DRM
People depending on a standard battery life of several days without configuration
Users looking for a ready-to-use device guaranteed without distribution configuration
content.verdict: Plasma Mobile is an open mobile environment for the Linux world, which transposes the KDE ecosystem onto smartphones with a Wayland architecture and a convergent framework.

components.note: "The interface is using KWin over Wayland and is now mostly stable, albeit a little rough around the edges in some areas." (plasma-mobile.org/about).
